Elena / Maya — thanks for the questions. Summary answers below and attached evidence. I also included a DocuSign link where our redlined DPA is staged for Aurora review.

Quick answers: 
- Fallback if SCCs are invalidated: Redwood commits to an ICA-based contractual fallback combined with an immediate documented transfer impact assessment. For customers requiring an alternative, we offer (1) Dedicated deployment contracts to restrict data residency, or (2) a hosted DPF-compliant flow we can engage in with the customer to pursue recognized transfer mechanisms. Implementation timeline: standard ICA execution within 10 business days once mutual terms are agreed; Dedicated deployment timelines vary by region (typically 4–8 weeks).
- SOC 2: period: Jan 1 2025 — Dec 31 2025; auditor: Lumen Assurance LLP. SOC 2 summary attached (soc2-type2-summary.pdf). Full report available under NDA — contact Laura for next steps.
- KMS / key rotation: keys rotated on a 90-day cycle by default; we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration for Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted customers, keys are tenant-isolated within our cloud KMS; see kms-integration-summary.txt for details.
- Data retention / model caching: production KV caches are short-lived (max 24 hours for inference-level caches). Persistent logging for debugging is retained for 30 days by default and is configurable; we do not use customer prompts to train upstream models unless explicitly contracted (we provide an opt-out in the DPA).
